correctness.rationale: For every \(N\ge3\) tree and arbitrary positive edge costs, Cauchy–Schwarz gives the unique base-tree optimum \(g_e=\sqrt{b_e/c_e}/S\) with \(K=S^2\). The rank-one Kirchhoff-index derivative is \(-N\|L^+\beta\|_2^2\). Unit-current potentials are cut-indicator sums weighted by \(S\sqrt{c_e/b_e}\), giving the exact derivative \(-S^2\Theta\). Nested-cut covariance yields the closed threshold and off-path price locality. Strict convexity of the trace-inverse on the connected simple-graph conductance domain gives the global if-and-only-if and unique equality case. For the two-hop classification, the components have positive orders \(a,b,k\) with \(a+b+k=N\): the minimum is at \(a=b=1\); the maximum is at \(k=1\) with balanced \(a,b\). The exact script checks 154 rational trees and all integer two-hop size profiles for \(3\le N\le49\), supplementing rather than replacing the infinite proof. Tree edges can have zero weight in the new optimum when a chord is installed; the theorem does not exclude this.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is an explicit all-tree arbitrary-price shortcut purchase theorem, strong off-path price-locality and a complete sharp finite-N two-hop extremal window. General convexity/KKT/tree weights, path-only unit-price special cases and fixed-base link insertion are identified as antecedents, not counted. Primary full-text comparison did not reveal equivalent closed formulas. A historical direct specialization or the inaccessible contemporary preprint may still affect novelty; no search result certifies uniqueness.
residual_risks: A direct earlier specialization of the known 2008 tree formula and general KKT could be expressed in different algebraic language; searching is not a completeness proof.

value.rationale: A natural edge-purchase decision under a single physical conductance budget is reduced for every tree and arbitrary positive prices to a computable closed form on one path; varying prices elsewhere provably cannot alter the decision. A strict sharp universal length-dependent cost bound and complete attained finite-order two-hop topology extrema show nontrivial structural effects beyond an isolated example or a numerical re-solution of a general SDP. This precisely motivated classification can guide link procurement without solving an augmented convex program. It neither claims a downstream theorem nor pretends that a formula alone establishes originality.
